quests.instruction: ARRANGE THE EMAIL PARTS INTO THE CORRECT ORDER
quests.prompt: The CEO has 30 seconds before a board meeting. Frame: Subject: Decision needed today: supplier contract / Greeting: Dear Ms Abara, / Sign-off: Regards, Neil. Arrange the body so she can act without opening the attachment.
options: Legal has reviewed it, and the only open point is a 60-day termination clause, which I consider acceptable.
Please approve the Dunmore contract today, as their price offer expires at 5 pm.
The full contract is attached if you would like to read it.
The contract is £412,000 over three years, which is 9% below our current spend.
quests.hint: Ask what she must do, and what she needs to feel safe doing it. The attachment is optional.
quests.explanation: The first line gives the action and the deadline. The next two lines answer the questions a cautious executive would ask: cost and risk. The attachment is offered last as optional.

quests.instruction: ARRANGE THE EMAIL PARTS INTO THE CORRECT ORDER
quests.prompt: Assemble the body of an email to your team that combines an urgent request with less urgent information. The subject is 'Please read: client visit tomorrow at 9 am'; the greeting is 'Hi all,'; the sign-off is 'Thanks, Gwen'.
options: The client is interested in our security processes, so please be ready to answer questions about them.
The slides from the meeting are in the usual folder.
Reception will be moved to the second floor for the visit, and lunch is arranged for 12:30.
Please make sure your desks are clear and your screens locked before you leave tonight, as the client will walk through the office at 9 am.
quests.hint: Which part of the message could cause harm if missed? Put that first.
quests.explanation: The action needed tonight is time-critical, so it leads. Logistics and expectations follow, and a routine pointer to slides goes last.

quests.instruction: ARRANGE THE EMAIL PARTS INTO THE CORRECT ORDER
quests.prompt: Lay out the email so that a busy mentor can answer in one line.
options: I need to reply by Friday, and I'd value your view on whether early-career mentoring matters more than salary.

A one-line answer would be extremely helpful; I know you're busy.

Thank you,
Cristiano
Subject: Quick question: should I accept the Lisbon offer?

Hi Professor Castellano,

I have two job offers: one in Lisbon (higher pay) and one in Leeds (better mentoring).
quests.hint: The mentor's time is short. What would let her answer easily?
quests.explanation: The subject holds the question, and the choice is described briefly. Asking for a one-line answer lowers the effort required and shows respect.

quests.instruction: ARRANGE THE EMAIL PARTS INTO THE CORRECT ORDER
quests.prompt: You must decline a job offer from a senior contact who helped you get an interview. The subject line, greeting and sign-off are already written (Subject: Thank you, and my decision on the Operations role / Dear Mr Kaplan, / Yours sincerely, Sheila Rao). Arrange the body.
options: After careful thought, I have decided to accept another position that is closer to my long-term interests.
I want to thank you again for the introduction, which meant a great deal to me, and for the time your team spent with me.
I hope our paths will cross again, and I will always be grateful for your support.
So I must decline your offer.
quests.hint: Gratitude before news, then the decision, then a positive note about the future.
quests.explanation: When someone has helped you, the appreciation must come before the refusal. Giving a broad reason avoids criticising them, and the future-oriented ending protects the relationship.

quests.instruction: ARRANGE THE EMAIL PARTS INTO THE CORRECT ORDER
quests.prompt: A friend's business idea seems weak. The subject line, greeting and sign-off are already written (Subject: Re: Your café idea / Hi Kamal, / Best of luck whatever you decide, Pia). Arrange the body.
options: I can see how much it means to you.
If it would help, I could go through the budget with you this weekend.
I do have some concerns about rent costs on that street, and I would want to see the numbers before you commit your savings.
Thank you for telling me about the café idea.
quests.hint: Support the person, name the concern with a reason, offer help.
quests.explanation: Honest doubt is easier to hear when it is specific and paired with an offer to help. Ending with support respects his right to decide.

quests.instruction: ARRANGE THE EMAIL PARTS INTO THE CORRECT ORDER
quests.prompt: The subject line, greeting and sign-off are already written (Subject: Re: Your request for promotion / Dear Danielle, / Kind regards, Charles). Arrange the body.
options: Thank you for raising this.
I would like to help you gain this by giving you the campaign budget from October, and we can review your progress in January.
I know it took courage, and I want to respond honestly.
At the moment I am unable to recommend a promotion because the role requires experience managing budgets.
quests.hint: Recognise the courage, give the honest reason, provide a route to the goal.
quests.explanation: A refusal with a development path reads as an investment. The reason is specific and doesn't attack her ability.

quests.instruction: ARRANGE THE EMAIL PARTS INTO THE CORRECT ORDER
quests.prompt: You have already answered a question twice, and the same person asks again. Build a reply that avoids sounding irritated.
options: Hi Jamie,
Thanks for checking. It's worth confirming these things, and I know there's been a lot of information going around.

The workshop starts on Monday 14 July at 10 am in Room 4, and I'll put the details in a short note at the top of the shared page so they're easy to find.

Best,
Colleen
Subject: Re: Opening date of the workshop
quests.hint: Which order gives the answer politely and prevents future repetition?
quests.explanation: Starting with reassurance avoids the implied 'I already told you'. Solving the underlying problem (information hard to find) is more constructive than repeating the fact.

quests.instruction: ARRANGE THE EMAIL PARTS INTO THE CORRECT ORDER
quests.prompt: Rewrite the order of an email that follows up on a missed reply so that it doesn't sound accusing.
options:
If the timing isn't right, that's completely fine, but could you let me know whether it's still under consideration?

Thanks very much,
Cyrus
I know things have been busy, so I wanted to check in on the proposal I sent on 2 June.
Subject: Checking in on the proposal
Hi Neha,
quests.hint: Cushion the follow-up, then ask, leaving an easy exit.
quests.explanation: Words such as 'I know things have been busy' avoid the implication that she has been negligent. Offering an easy exit encourages a reply even if the answer is no.

quests.instruction: ARRANGE THE EMAIL PARTS INTO THE CORRECT ORDER
quests.prompt: Arrange the email that gives negative feedback to a supplier without insulting them.
options:
The last three deliveries have arrived up to two days after the agreed date, and this has started to affect our own customers. Could we discuss what has changed and how we can put it right?

Yours sincerely,
Martha Ito
Dear Mr Zhou,
We have valued your company's reliability over the years, which is why I wanted to raise a concern directly with you.
Subject: Feedback on the last three deliveries
quests.hint: Value the partnership first; report the pattern; invite a discussion.
quests.explanation: Beginning with appreciation shows the concern is not an attack. Using facts and asking 'what has changed' invites cooperation.

quests.instruction: ARRANGE THE EMAIL PARTS INTO THE CORRECT ORDER
quests.prompt: The message must be under fifty words. Lay out the four pieces of a very short request to a colleague.
options:
Hi Femi,

Could I borrow Room 3 tomorrow from 2 to 3 pm for a client call?

Thanks,
Polly
Subject: Room 3 tomorrow, 2 pm?
I can swap with your team on Friday if you need it then.
quests.hint: Every word must earn its place. What is the request, and what makes it easy to agree?
quests.explanation: Short emails still need purpose, timing and an incentive. The subject already contains the room and time, so the body needs no repetition.

quests.instruction: ARRANGE THE EMAIL PARTS INTO THE CORRECT ORDER
quests.prompt: Piece together a brief reply confirming you have received documents.
options: The countersigned copy will be with you by Thursday.
Subject: Re: Signed contract received

Dear Ms Barkley,

Thank you: I confirm that we received the signed contract this morning.

Kind regards,
Steven
quests.hint: Confirmation, next step; nothing else.
quests.explanation: A receipt confirmation should be one clear line. Adding what happens next tells the recipient when to expect the countersigned copy.

quests.instruction: ARRANGE THE EMAIL PARTS INTO THE CORRECT ORDER
quests.prompt: Set out a short email that turns down an invitation with no explanation but with warmth.
options: Subject: Re: Your leaving drinks

Warm wishes,
Edmund
I'm sorry I can't join you, but I wish you every happiness in the new job.

Dear Beatrice,

Thank you so much for the invitation to your leaving drinks.
quests.hint: Thanks, decline, kind wish.
quests.explanation: You are not obliged to give a reason for declining a social invitation. Wishing them well makes the refusal feel warm, not cold.

quests.instruction: ARRANGE THE EMAIL PARTS INTO THE CORRECT ORDER
quests.prompt: You are explaining a system outage to non-technical customers. Frame: Subject: Our service was interrupted this morning / Greeting: Dear customers, / Sign-off: Yours sincerely, The Support Team. Arrange the body.
options: We are sorry for the trouble; if you still cannot log in, please contact us.
Between 9 and 10:30 am today, you may have been unable to log in to your account.
The problem has now been fixed, and no personal information was affected.
It was caused by a fault in the equipment that manages logins, which we have replaced.
quests.hint: Customers want to know what they experienced, whether it is fixed, and whether they are safe. The technical cause matters less.
quests.explanation: Non-technical readers need impact and reassurance before cause. A short explanation follows for those who wonder why.

quests.instruction: ARRANGE THE EMAIL PARTS INTO THE CORRECT ORDER
quests.prompt: You are explaining the same outage to the IT director. Frame: Subject: Incident report: login outage, 9:00 to 10:30 / Greeting: Dear Mr Owens, / Sign-off: Regards, Petra. Build the body.
options: Next steps: we will add a firmware test to the change process and review the failover time.
Impact: 4,200 users could not log in for 90 minutes, and no data was lost.
Root cause: the primary authentication server failed after a failed firmware update at 8:55.
Resolution: we failed over to the secondary server at 10:25 and replaced the primary at 11:40.
quests.hint: A technical director wants cause, impact, resolution and prevention.
quests.explanation: The same event is described differently for a specialist. Precision, cause and prevention matter here, where customers care about impact.

quests.instruction: ARRANGE THE EMAIL PARTS INTO THE CORRECT ORDER
quests.prompt: Put together an email introducing a technical change to colleagues from the sales team.
options: Hi sales team,
Subject: New customer database: what changes for you
From 1 September, you will use a new system to record customer calls, and it should save you about ten minutes a day.

You will log in with the same details as now. A short video showing you how to add a call is attached.

Best wishes,
Adriana
quests.hint: For non-specialists, start with what changes in their day.
quests.explanation: Sales staff care about how it affects their work, not the technology. A benefit and a reassuring detail make change easier.

quests.instruction: ARRANGE THE EMAIL PARTS INTO THE CORRECT ORDER
quests.prompt: A contact has ignored two emails about a signed agreement. The subject line, greeting and sign-off are already written (Subject: Third request: signed agreement needed by Friday 27 June / Dear Mr Balogun, / Yours sincerely, Rhiannon Goldberg). Arrange the body so that it is firm and courteous.
options: I have written twice, on 10 and 17 June, asking for the signed partnership agreement, and I haven't yet received a reply.
So please send it by Friday 27 June.
If there is any issue with the terms, please let me know so that we can resolve it.
We cannot start work until we have it.
quests.hint: History, consequence, deadline, and openness to hear about a problem.
quests.explanation: The message is firm because it has dates, a consequence and a deadline. It is polite because it allows for a legitimate reason for the delay.

quests.instruction: ARRANGE THE EMAIL PARTS INTO THE CORRECT ORDER
quests.prompt: A neighbour has ignored requests to stop leaving bins in a shared passage. The subject line, greeting and sign-off are already written (Subject: Bins in the shared passage / Dear Mr and Mrs Coleman, / Kind regards, Dominic Reyes). Arrange the body.
options: They block the fire exit for flats 5 and 6.
If this continues, I will need to inform the managing agent.
So I must ask you to keep them in your own yard from now on.
I wanted to write again about the bins in the shared passage, which I mentioned to you in April and June.
quests.hint: Refer to previous requests, explain the safety reason, state the next step calmly.
quests.explanation: The safety reason makes the request reasonable. Naming the next step is honest, not a threat.

quests.instruction: ARRANGE THE EMAIL PARTS INTO THE CORRECT ORDER
quests.prompt: Piece together the email declining to reopen a settled agreement while remaining respectful.
options:
We agreed the terms of the lease in March, and I am not able to reopen them at this stage. I would be willing to discuss a break clause at the renewal date if that would help.

Yours sincerely,
Graham Cutts
Subject: Re: Request to renegotiate the lease terms
Thank you for your message, and I appreciate that circumstances have changed for you.
Dear Ms Dufresne,
quests.hint: Empathy, firm position, and a limited concession later.
quests.explanation: Being clear about what will not change avoids false hope. The future offer shows goodwill.

quests.instruction: ARRANGE THE EMAIL PARTS INTO THE CORRECT ORDER
quests.prompt: A customer asks something that is answered on the website. The subject line, greeting and sign-off are already written (Subject: Re: How do I change my delivery address? / Dear Mrs Engstrom, / Kind regards, Isaac Bolton). Arrange the body.
options: Thank you for getting in touch, and I'm happy to help.
You can change your address under 'My Account' and 'Delivery details'.
If you'd rather, I can update it for you now if you send me the new address.
I have attached a screenshot showing exactly where to click.
quests.hint: Answer first, then offer to do it for them.
quests.explanation: A helpful reply solves the problem and avoids saying 'It's on our website'. Offering to do it removes the burden.

quests.instruction: ARRANGE THE EMAIL PARTS INTO THE CORRECT ORDER
quests.prompt: A student asks a question already in the syllabus. Structure your reply.
options: Dear Ali,
Thanks for your question.
Subject: Re: Assessment dates

The two assignments are due on 14 November and 12 December, and you'll find them on page 3 of the module guide as well. If any of the dates clash with other commitments, do tell me early.

Best wishes,
Dr Fenwick
quests.hint: Answer plainly; avoid 'as stated in the guide'.
quests.explanation: Answering directly is respectful. A mention of the guide is a pointer, not a reproach.

quests.instruction: ARRANGE THE EMAIL PARTS INTO THE CORRECT ORDER
quests.prompt: The subject line, greeting and sign-off are already written (Subject: Quick check on the reporting process / Hi Rowena, / Best, Etienne). Arrange the body.
options: Sorry if you explained this at the last meeting.
Do we send the monthly report to Finance before or after the manager signs it off?
But I want to be sure I get it right.
Thanks for bearing with me.
quests.hint: Preface the question with humility; then ask.
quests.explanation: Acknowledging that you may be repeating a question shows consideration. It also reduces the chance of an irritated response.

quests.instruction: ARRANGE THE EMAIL PARTS INTO THE CORRECT ORDER
quests.prompt: You do not yet know when a fault will be fixed. Put together an update that is honest and still useful.
options: The lift has been out of service since Monday, and I am sorry for the difficulty this causes.
Subject: Update on the lift repair at Ridgeway House

At the moment, we do not know when it will be repaired, because the engineer is waiting for a part with no confirmed delivery date. I will update you on Friday, or sooner if there is news, and in the meantime we can arrange help with shopping for anyone who needs it.

Yours sincerely,
Patricia Odum, Building Manager
Dear residents,
quests.hint: What is known, what is not, when you'll say more, and what you can do now.
quests.explanation: Saying plainly what you do not know builds trust, and a date for the next update prevents repeated enquiries. Practical help shows care.

quests.instruction: ARRANGE THE EMAIL PARTS INTO THE CORRECT ORDER
quests.prompt: Assemble the email to a client about a project result that is not yet certain.
options: The first three weeks of the trial suggest that the new process may reduce waiting times by 10 to 15%.

These figures are provisional, because we have only tested it at one site, and we should not draw firm conclusions yet. We will have results from all three sites by 30 July.

Yours sincerely,
Saoirse Popescu
Subject: Early results from the trial: cautious progress
Dear Dr Ncube,
quests.hint: State the finding, then its limits, then when certainty will come.
quests.explanation: Presenting a finding with appropriate caution avoids overpromising. The date for full results manages expectations.

quests.instruction: ARRANGE THE EMAIL PARTS INTO THE CORRECT ORDER
quests.prompt: The subject line, greeting and sign-off are already written (Subject: What I know, and what I don't yet know / Dear team, / Sincerely, Roberta). Arrange the body.
options: I do not yet know whether any roles are affected, and I will tell you as soon as I can.
I know that the company is reviewing costs, and that decisions will be made in September.
My door is open at any time.
I understand you are worried about the announcement, so I want to be as open as I can.
quests.hint: Empathy, known facts, unknowns, commitment.
quests.explanation: Separating what you know from what you don't is more honest than vague reassurance. A commitment to share information is comforting.

quests.instruction: ARRANGE THE EMAIL PARTS INTO THE CORRECT ORDER
quests.prompt: You are a stranger emailing a busy journalist with a story idea. Arrange the email so she reads to the end.
options:
Dear Ms Okoro,

Three villages in North Devon will lose their only bus service on 1 September, affecting roughly 900 residents.
Subject: Story idea: three villages losing their only bus route

I know you cover rural transport, and I thought this might interest you.

I can send the figures today if you would like them.

Yours sincerely,
Harold Peters
I am a local councillor, and I have data showing that no consultation took place, along with residents willing to speak on the record.
quests.hint: Lead with what is newsworthy. Say who you are only after you've caught attention.
quests.explanation: The subject and first line hold the story. Your credentials and the offer come after, so the reader can decide quickly.

quests.instruction: ARRANGE THE EMAIL PARTS INTO THE CORRECT ORDER
quests.prompt: Set out the email from a job seeker to a stranger at a company they admire.
options: Subject: Question about product design at Lumen

If you have time for a brief reply, I would be very grateful; either way, thank you for considering it.

Kind regards,
Asha Menon

Dear Mr Tsai,

I have followed Lumen's design work since your redesign of the mobile app last year.
I am a product designer with four years' experience and would like to ask a single question about how your team tests early prototypes.
quests.hint: A single, easy question is more likely to get an answer than a request for a job.
quests.explanation: A small request from a stranger has a better chance. Showing knowledge of their work makes the email personal.

quests.instruction: ARRANGE THE EMAIL PARTS INTO THE CORRECT ORDER
quests.prompt: Structure an email from a small business owner offering services to a large company.
options: I would like to offer your team a free tasting for your September events.
Subject: Local catering for your staff events

Dear Ms Reyes,

I run a family catering business that specialises in healthy meals for offices, and we already serve three companies in your building.

If this would be of interest, I can visit any day next week.

Kind regards,
Jorge Alvarez
quests.hint: A cold pitch should give a reason to reply and a low-risk offer.
quests.explanation: Mentioning neighbours gives credibility. A free tasting is a small step for the reader.

quests.instruction: ARRANGE THE EMAIL PARTS INTO THE CORRECT ORDER
quests.prompt: Two managers have given you conflicting instructions. Frame: Subject: Two conflicting priorities: your guidance please / Greeting: Dear Ms Barker and Mr Ito, / Sign-off: Kind regards, Leona. Build the body so neither feels criticised.
options: Could you agree between you which should come first and let me know by tomorrow noon?
Ms Barker has asked me to finish the pricing review by Friday, and Mr Ito has asked me to prepare the board slides by the same day.
I can complete one by Friday and the other by Tuesday, but not both by Friday.
I would like to deliver what you both need, and I want to check how to prioritise.
quests.hint: State your intention, describe the conflict neutrally, offer options, and request a joint decision.
quests.explanation: Presenting the situation neutrally avoids putting either manager in the wrong. Asking them to agree between themselves puts the responsibility in the right place.

quests.instruction: ARRANGE THE EMAIL PARTS INTO THE CORRECT ORDER
quests.prompt: A client and your own manager want different things. The subject line, greeting and sign-off are already written (Subject: Client request that conflicts with our policy / Dear Ms Farah, / Kind regards, Benedict). Arrange the body.
options: Could you let me know by Wednesday?
A client has asked us to waive the cancellation fee for their event, which our policy doesn't allow.
I would suggest offering a 50% reduction as a one-off, but I want your approval before I reply.
They have been loyal for six years and spend about £40,000 a year.
quests.hint: Issue, context that matters, your recommendation, decision request.
quests.explanation: Giving the client's value provides context for an exception. Asking for approval first respects your manager's authority.

quests.instruction: ARRANGE THE EMAIL PARTS INTO THE CORRECT ORDER
quests.prompt: The subject line, greeting and sign-off are already written (Subject: Customer request for weekend work / Dear Mr Fofanah, / Kind regards, Aisling Hart). Arrange the body.
options: Our developers have already worked three weekends this quarter, so we cannot ask them to work another.
We can bring in two extra contractors on Saturday instead, at your agreed daily rate, and keep the launch on the 14th.
Shall I go ahead?
Thank you for explaining how important the launch date is to your team.
quests.hint: Understand the need, explain the limit honestly, offer a solution that meets both.
quests.explanation: Explaining the limit as care for the team is honest and respectable. A concrete alternative keeps the client's date.
